settings.notify.title: Notifications
settings.notify.help: A system notice when a quota resets, per the time the provider reported. Sent by the app while it runs (also hidden in the tray), once per reset; no extra query is made, the new balance shows on the next refresh.
settings.notify.denied: The system did not allow notifications from Cuotai, so the option stays off.
settings.notify.system: Open the system settings → Notifications, allow Cuotai and turn the option on again. Use “Send test notification” to check.
settings.notify.whenHelp: Windows of 5 hours, a day, a week or a month; rate limits and balances never notify.
settings.alerts.help: A system notice when a quota with a limit reaches a threshold of use, once per threshold and window; also hidden in the tray, never with the app closed and with no extra query. Balances, spend and rate limits never alert.
settings.alerts.thresholdsHelp: Share of the quota used, from {min} to {max}%. Click a threshold to remove it.
settings.alerts.overageHelp: When an account starts paying for extra usage, once per billing cycle; with exhaustion on, also when the extra budget runs out.
settings.notify.accounts: Each account has a bell on its card and in its details that turns its reset notices and usage alerts on or off; in the details, each quota can also mute its own alerts. The choices are saved per provider and account name: renaming the account turns them back on.
settings.notify.testSent: Test notification sent. If it did not appear, allow Cuotai in the system notification settings.
settings.notify.testFailed: The test notification could not be sent.
notify.test.title: Cuotai: test notification
notify.test.body: Cuotai notices will look like this.

card.extra.title: Extra usage
settings.group.help: Accounts with a used-up quota move to a collapsible group with their return time. Display only: the manual order inside each group and the order saved in the file stay as they are.
settings.pace.help: Compares what was used with a steady pace until the reset and says whether it lasts. A linear estimate, not a promise; windows that just opened show nothing.
settings.history.title: History
settings.history.help: Each successful reading is recorded on this computer only (numbers and windows, never credentials or provider text). Older samples are thinned to one per hour after 7 days and the file stays under 64 MiB.
settings.history.eraseAll: Erase the whole measurement history on this computer, for every configuration? This cannot be undone.
settings.history.eraseOne: Erase the measurement history of {account}? This cannot be undone.
settings.history.stale: The accounts changed. Choose the account again.
settings.history.recordHelp: Off: nothing new is recorded, and what was already recorded stays (kept for the days below) until you erase it. Applies to this app; the terminal and the command line still record.
settings.history.size: On disk: {size} (the whole history on this computer).

trend.noUsed: No measured use in this period.

settings.order.title: Account order

dialog.session.confirmHint: Click again to confirm: the variable's value goes to the system vault and the variable leaves the TOML.
dialog.session.migrated: Session moved to the system vault. Remove the variable from your environment whenever you like.

settings.privacy.title: Privacy
settings.status.help: Off by default. When on, Cuotai makes public requests to the status pages of the providers you configured, at most once every 5 minutes per page, without credentials, cookies or account data. Those sites can see your IP address and that you use the provider. Incidents appear on the cards and on the tray icon.
settings.status.none: None of your configured providers has a verified status page; nothing would be queried.
settings.serve.title: Integration
settings.serve.help: A read-only local server lets status bars and scripts read your usage (/v1/snapshot, /v1/limits, /v1/accounts/{key}, /health) in the export v1 format. It serves this app's own readings: reading it never queries a provider.
settings.serve.cuotaiOnPort: Another Cuotai server (such as cuotai --serve) is already using port {port}: stop it or choose another port here.
settings.serve.portHelp: Default {port}, from {min} to {max}. Exactly this port is used: when it is taken, the server stays off and says so.
settings.serve.token.title: Access token
settings.serve.token.on: Every request must send Authorization: Bearer <token>. The token is kept in the system vault, never in cuotai.toml, and is never shown: copy it into your client.
settings.serve.token.off: No token: any program running as you on this computer can read the server; web pages are still refused.
settings.serve.token.revokeHelp: A new token stops the old one at once. Revoking removes it from the vault, and the server answers without a token again.
settings.serve.browsersOff: Off: requests from web pages are refused and no page can read the answers.
settings.serve.privacy: It only listens on this computer (127.0.0.1) and never serves credentials. Any program running under your user can read what it serves, as with cuotai --json.
serve.banner: The local server is not serving:
settings.widgets.title: Widgets
settings.widgets.help: Publishes a small JSON file with what the app already shows (the binding quota of each account, its age and freshness), written atomically and readable only by your user. Widgets and third-party panels (Waybar, GNOME, KDE) read that file; nothing queries a provider.
settings.widgets.off: Off: no file is written and an existing one is deleted.
settings.widgets.onState: On: the file is rewritten after each change, at most once every 15 seconds.
settings.widgets.identityHelp: Off by default: the e-mail of each account stays out of the file, and no note or credential ever enters it.
settings.widgets.maxAccountsHelp: From {min} to {max}. The most restrictive accounts come first; the rest are not published.
settings.widgets.path.label: File location
settings.widgets.path.appGroup: App group container: the WidgetKit extension reads this file.
settings.widgets.path.userDataMac: This user's data directory: panels and scripts read it, but a WidgetKit extension needs the signed app first.
settings.widgets.path.userData: This user's local data directory: panels and scripts read it.
settings.widgets.redraw: The operating system decides when a widget redraws and may keep the last data; the age shown always belongs to the reading it came from.
settings.widgets.macos: On macOS the widget extension additionally needs an Apple developer account, the app group entitlement and a provisioning profile in the signed app (PRD 0019). Without them only third-party integrations can read the file.
settings.hooks.title: Hooks
settings.hooks.help: Hooks run commands of your own when something happens to an account (a quota crosses a threshold, runs out or resets, a query fails…), detected from this app's own readings, so they add no query. The command gets the event as JSON on its standard input and in CUOTAI_EVENT, CUOTAI_ACCOUNT, CUOTAI_PROVIDER and CUOTAI_METRIC, runs without a shell and inherits only PATH, HOME and LANG. The rules live in hooks.toml next to the accounts' file, shared with cuotai --watch --hooks.

settings.hooks.state.on.one: On: 1 rule runs on its events.
settings.hooks.state.on.other: On: {count} rules run on their events.

settings.hooks.state.unconfirmed: Waiting for your confirmation: the rules are new or changed since you confirmed them, so nothing runs.
settings.hooks.state.missing: No rules yet: add one below and save it.
settings.hooks.state.noConfig: Hooks need an accounts file; choose or create one first.
settings.hooks.unparsable: hooks.toml is not a TOML file the editor can show; fix it in a text editor.
settings.hooks.name: Name
settings.hooks.commandHelp: One field per argument, passed exactly as written: no shell, no ~ or variables. The first is the program: an absolute path (/usr/local/bin/notify) or a name looked up in PATH.
settings.hooks.testHelp: Run this rule now with a sample event (marked "sample": true in the payload).
settings.hooks.testOff: Save the rule, turn hooks on and confirm it to test it.
settings.hooks.testSent: Sample event sent to {name}; its run shows below when it ends.
settings.hooks.runs.title: Latest runs
settings.hooks.confirm.title: Confirm hook commands
settings.hooks.confirm.help: Cuotai will run exactly these commands, as your user, whenever the listed events happen. Confirm only commands you know and trust; any change to the rules asks again.
settings.hooks.event.quota_exhaustion_pr: a quota may run out before the reset
settings.hooks.event.overage_started: paid extra usage started (once per billing cycle)
settings.hooks.event.session_expiring: a pasted session is about to expire
settings.cost.title: Local cost
settings.cost.help: Estimates, on this computer only, the tokens your command-line tools used, from their local logs. Off by default: each source first shows exactly what it will read and asks for confirmation. Conversation content is never read.
settings.cost.indexed: In the index: {files} log(s), {invalid} invalid line(s) ignored.
settings.cost.state.scanning: Reading what grew in the logs…
settings.cost.state.paused: Paused: the computer is saving energy; reading resumes when it stops.
settings.cost.eraseText: Erase the whole local cost index? Sources that stay on read their logs again from the start.
cost.card.title: Local usage · {source}
cost.card.estimate: Estimate at API prices on this computer, not a charge.
cost.solo.title: Local usage
cost.detail.title: Local usage of {source} on this computer
cost.detail.help: From the {source} logs on this computer: the same on every account of the tool, not this account's billing.
cost.detail.off: The {source} logs are not read, so nothing is shown. Turn the source on in Settings › Advanced › Local cost to see the tokens and the estimated cost at API prices.
cost.detail.chartCost: Estimated cost per day from {first} to {last}; highest: {peak} on {day}.
cost.detail.chartTokens: Tokens per day from {first} to {last} (no model with a price); highest: {peak} on {day}.
cost.tokens.breakdown: Input {input} · Output {output} · Cache read {cache_read} · Cache write 5 min {cache_write} · Cache write 1 h {cache_write_1h}
settings.cost.pathsHelp: One per line, absolute or starting with ~/. Empty: the defaults. A different list turns the source off until you review it again.
settings.cost.pathsSaved: Directories of {source} saved. Turn the source on to review what it will read.
settings.cost.pathsOffText: {source} was turned on for other directories. Changing them turns it off and erases everything derived from it; turn it on again to review the new directories.
settings.cost.pricesHelp: USD per million tokens. Nothing is downloaded: your pricing.json, edited by hand in the same format, wins over the embedded table model by model; an invalid file is ignored as a whole.
settings.cost.pricesUser: Your table: prices of {date}; source: {source}; {count} model(s) over the embedded table.
settings.cost.pricesMissing: You have no pricing.json; create it in the same format to review or change prices.
settings.cost.unknownModel: A model outside the table has an unknown cost, never zero.
settings.cost.confirm.title: Turn on reading {source}?
settings.cost.confirm.dirs: It reads only the {pattern} files of these directories, and nothing outside them:
settings.cost.disable.title: Turn {source} off?
settings.cost.disable.text: Reading stops and everything derived from the {source} logs is erased from the index.
hooks.banner.unconfirmed: Hooks are on, but their rules changed since you confirmed them: nothing runs until you review them.
hooks.banner.invalid: Hooks are on, but hooks.toml cannot be used.
extensions.title: Extensions
extensions.help: Discovered local extensions. Cuotai asks for consent before the first run and whenever executable content changes.
extensions.confirm: I reviewed every item above and accept the residual risk.
extensions.testFailed: The test did not return a usable report.
update.title: Updates
update.privacy: When checking, the app reads only the current version, the operating system and this computer's architecture, and compares them with a public list of releases. No account, usage, name or identifier is sent. You can turn the checks off below.
update.consent.title: Check for updates automatically?
update.consent.body: A check fetches GitHub's public release manifest. Your current version, operating system and computer architecture are compared with it locally and are not sent. No account, usage data, name or machine identifier is sent. Nothing downloads or installs without a click.
update.consent.pending: Answer the update question before checking.
update.state.uptodate: This version is up to date.
update.state.ready: Version {version} is ready; restart to finish.
update.off.preference: Turned off in the settings: no check is made.
update.off.env: Turned off by the environment's CUOTAI_UPDATER=off: this install's package manager updates it.
update.off.build: Turned off in this copy's build (packager build key).
update.off.homebrew: This copy was installed by Homebrew: update it with the command below.
update.off.scoop: This copy was installed by Scoop: update it with the command below.
update.off.winget: This copy was installed by winget: update it with the command below.
update.off.linux_package: This copy was installed by a system package: update it with the manager below.
update.off.cargo: This copy was installed by Cargo: update it with the command below.
update.off.other: This installation does not use the in-app updater.
update.cannot.managed: This installation is owned by a package manager; use the command below.
update.cannot.place: Cuotai cannot update itself from this location (a disk image or a read-only folder). Download it manually.
update.error.network: The release server could not be reached. You can download it manually.
update.error.signature: The package signature does not match the project's public key; nothing was installed. Download it manually and open an issue in the repository.
update.error.io: The installation could not be written (permission or disk space). You can download it manually.
update.error.insecure_endpoint: The check address is not HTTPS; the check was refused.
update.error.unconfigured: This copy was not built with the update channel.
update.error.other: The update failed. You can download it manually.

report.tooLong: This report is too long for a link: copy it and paste it into a new issue.
